page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: What PAR stands for
lines: It is the part of sunlight that green plants
steps.why: The expansion is one mark on its own, and the second line explains why only part of sunlight counts — a plant cannot use every wavelength that reaches it.
common_mistakes: Writing Photosynthetic Active Rays. The words are Photosynthetically Active Radiation.
Writing that PAR is all the sunlight that reaches the earth. It is only the usable part.
steps.memory_tip: Three words for three letters: Photosynthetically, Active, Radiation.
steps.margin_note: The expansion in full, then one line on what it means.

steps.label: How much of it

lines.text: PAR is under 50% of the incoming sunlight

lines: PAR is less than 50% of the incident solar
Of this PAR, green plants capture only
steps.why: Two different percentages are asked about PAR in this chapter and they are easily swapped, so both are written together with the word they belong to beside each.
common_mistakes: Writing that plants capture 50% of PAR. Fifty per cent is the share of SUNLIGHT that is PAR.
Giving 2 to 10% of sunlight. It is 2 to 10% of PAR, not of all the sunlight.
steps.memory_tip: Less than half the sunlight is PAR; only 2 to 10% of THAT is captured by plants.
steps.margin_note: Both numbers with the thing each one is a percentage of. Two lines.

insider_note: The two percentages belong to different quantities — under 50% of sunlight is PAR, and 2 to 10% of PAR is captured — and swapping them is the usual mistake.
